candidates.name: Marmot projects at bitcoin++ Seoul
candidates.reason: Top Stories: bitcoin++ Seoul, a privacy-themed Bitcoin developer conference held 5 and 6 November, ran a hackathon whose gallery lists 20 projects, several of them built on Marmot encrypted groups.

candidates.name: Nostur
candidates.reason: Tagged Releases: Nostur, an iOS and macOS client, adds polls in 1.35.0.

candidates.name: Monostr
candidates.reason: Tagged Releases: Monostr, a Nostr client built around Monero tips, builds in Tor in v0.34.0.

candidates.name: Chama
candidates.reason: Tagged Releases: Chama, a peer-to-peer bitcoin trading app with ecash escrow, closes the final open item from its security audit in v6.4.34.

candidates.name: Zapstore
candidates.reason: Tagged Releases: Zapstore, the Nostr-based Android app store, shipped 2.0.2 through 2.0.4 in three days.

candidates.name: Manent
candidates.reason: Tagged Releases: Manent, a private notes app that stores encrypted notes on Nostr relays, released v3.1.0.

candidates.name: Streets
candidates.reason: Tagged Releases: Streets, a Japanese web client, separates relay budgets in v1.24.0.

candidates.name: NoorNote
candidates.reason: Tagged Releases: NoorNote, a desktop Nostr client, checks Lightning invoices before paying a zap in v1.9.10.

candidates.name: Infans
candidates.reason: Tagged Releases: Infans, an Android baby tracker that backs up and syncs between parents through encrypted Nostr events, fixes disappearing timers in v2.4.3.

candidates.name: Amber
candidates.reason: Tagged Releases: Amber, an Android app that holds Nostr keys and signs for other apps, adds a local relay in v7.0.0-pre3, a pre-release.

candidates.name: Keep Android
candidates.reason: Tagged Releases: Keep Android, a FROST threshold signer, fixes several leaks in v1.4.0.

candidates.name: nostr-social-graph
candidates.reason: Tagged Releases: nostr-social-graph, a library that builds follow and mute graphs for Web of Trust scoring, changes its snapshot format in v4.0.0, after Newsletter #45 covered 3.0.0.

candidates.name: MDK
candidates.reason: Tagged Releases: MDK, the SDK and runtime for Marmot encrypted groups, released v0.15.0 together with MarmotKit bindings for iOS, macOS and Android.

candidates.name: Vector
candidates.reason: Tagged Releases: Vector, a private messenger built on Nostr, shipped v0.5.0 and v0.5.1.

candidates.name: Route96
candidates.reason: In Development: Route96, a media server for Blossom (hash-addressed media storage) and NIP-96 (HTTP file storage) uploads, merged security fixes on 8 November that are not yet in a tagged release.

candidates.name: SplitNut
candidates.reason: New Projects: SplitNut, from BlackIce's author, runs a stock Cashu mint whose signing keys are split two-of-three across guardians who coordinate in a Marmot group.

candidates.name: Moranduba
candidates.reason: New Projects: Moranduba is a Flutter group chat with end-to-end encrypted video calls and screen sharing, built on Marmot.

candidates.name: NIP-01 relays can tell clients how long to back off
candidates.reason: Protocol and Spec Work: A merged NIP-01 change adds an optional last parameter to the `OK` and `CLOSED` relay messages in NIP-01 (the base relay protocol).

candidates.name: NIP-47 logout method proposed
candidates.reason: Protocol and Spec Work: An open pull request adds a `logout` method to NIP-47, the Nostr Wallet Connect spec for controlling a wallet over Nostr.

candidates.name: Logout mirrored in the NWC specs repository
candidates.reason: Protocol and Spec Work: The same author opened a matching logout draft in the Nostr Wallet Connect specs.

candidates.name: Push registration for wallet notifications
candidates.reason: Protocol and Spec Work: A separate open NWC draft defines `register_push` and `unregister_push`, letting a client hand the wallet service a Web Push endpoint, which UnifiedPush distributors can also serve.

candidates.name: Concord merges Roles, private channels and voice
candidates.reason: Protocol and Spec Work: Concord is a protocol for encrypted Nostr communities.

candidates.name: Concord joins authenticate the community root
candidates.reason: Protocol and Spec Work: A Concord proposal covered in the August 19 issue (Newsletter #36) has now merged.

candidates.name: Marmot: moved devices keep trusting the old group until the first Commit
candidates.reason: Protocol and Spec Work: Marmot, the end-to-end encrypted group messaging protocol built on MLS and Nostr, merged five device-group and departure changes between 4 and 9 November.

candidates.name: Marmot: reset a local device group without losing chats
candidates.reason: Protocol and Spec Work: A device link can disappear from a device group's roster.

candidates.name: Marmot: inactive sibling devices
candidates.reason: Protocol and Spec Work: After 30 days of caught-up inactivity, a device marks a sibling device `inactive`.

candidates.name: Marmot: last active admin cannot leave
candidates.reason: Protocol and Spec Work: Under a departure rule, a leaving admin repeats its step-down while another admin remains.

candidates.name: Marmot: admins step down before leaving
candidates.reason: Protocol and Spec Work: A refused or lost step-down could stall a leave.

candidates.name: Marmot drafts one-shot agent decisions
candidates.reason: Protocol and Spec Work: An open draft specifies one-shot agent decisions: a software agent in an encrypted group asks one question and gets one answer, as ordinary encrypted group messages.

candidates.name: NIP-D9 proposes events that resist deletion
candidates.reason: Protocol and Spec Work: An open NIP-D9 proposal lets an author mark a regular event with a `no_delete` tag, exempting it from that author's own NIP-09 (deletion requests) and NIP-62 (request to vanish) requests, even if the request arrives first.

candidates.name: NIP Deep Dive: NIP-88 (Polls)
candidates.reason: NIP Deep Dive: NIP-88 (Polls): NIP-88: Polls lets anyone post a public poll that any client can count from events on ordinary relays, without a poll service.
